task.instruction: Choose exactly one owner of regional retry cadence for the next release: the platform team or regional teams. Shared approval and hybrid authority are unavailable. Give the boundary, rollback, escalation rule, and decision rationale. Cite the supplied evidence IDs.

evidence.content: There are four regions. Region C used five extra retries and conversion rose 4.2 percentage points.
Shared-IP complaints rose from .4% to 1.6%, above the 1.0% provider throttle threshold; other regions lost 7% delivery and throttle lasted 90 minutes.

The central complaint budget is .8%; each region has a kill switch; rollback takes six minutes. The control plane can assign final retry-cadence authority to exactly one owner for the release, with no shared approval or override.
A prior local change gained 3 points while shared-queue latency rose 18%.
A prior delegated change had a hard CPU budget and no cross-team effect for 60 days.

nondiagnostic_target_a.content: 2026-01-15 — Decision: Route the 3-point local change through shared-queue review. Reason: An 18% latency rise makes the cross-team cost a portfolio decision. Evidence: [ra-s3d-prior-01].

2026-02-12 — Decision: Leave CPU tuning with the service owner under its hard budget. Reason: Sixty spillover-free days make local evidence actionable and reversibility credible. Evidence: [ra-s3d-prior-02].

nondiagnostic_target_b.content: 2026-01-15 — Decision: Let the local owner retry under a temporary queue ceiling. Reason: The 3-point gain remains testable while the 18% shared cost is capped. Evidence: [ra-s3d-prior-01].
2026-02-12 — Decision: Keep quarterly review of the delegated CPU budget. Reason: Sixty spillover-free days still require shared visibility before envelope changes. Evidence: [ra-s3d-prior-02].
